intended_object: The T₂.₅ (Urysohn) separation axiom: any two distinct points have open neighbourhoods whose closures are disjoint. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The two filters (𝓝 x).lift' closure and (𝓝 y).lift' closure are disjoint exactly when some neighbourhood N of x and some neighbourhood M of y have disjoint closures. This is equivalent to the textbook definition with open sets. In one direction, N and M contain open sets U ∋ x and V ∋ y, and closure is monotone, so the closures of U and V are also disjoint. In the other direction, open sets containing x and y are neighbourhoods of those points. The definition is stated for an arbitrary topological space with no extra T₁ hypothesis, which is the natural generality; T₂.₅ already implies T₂. It is Mathlib's own definition of the notion.
